checked_sources: Independent exact cyclotomic determinant enumeration of all 40,401 translation-orbit pairs in check_f15.py
correctness.rationale: For every two five-subsets of Z/15Z, independent translations preserve Fourier rank by nonzero diagonal factors. All 3003 five-subsets partition into 200 translation orbits of length 15 and one length 3, giving 201x201 cases. Independently recomputed the characteristic-zero ranks from signed determinant polynomials in Z[X]/Phi_15 with Phi_15=X^8-X^7+X^5-X^4+X^3-X+1, checking successively minors 5,4,3,2. Reproduced exact weighted totals (rank 2: 360; rank 3: 24480; rank 4: 880920; rank 5: 8112249), summing to 9,018,009; independent parsed certificate also has these totals and symmetric table. Exactly eight representative pairs have rank 2 and all have the H={0,3,6,9,12} coset/two-residue-class form. The direct analytic construction counts 2*3*60=360 such pairs; hence the observed exhaustive table establishes converse. Rank 1 is excluded because nontrivial row/column difference annihilators of a 15-point character pairing cannot both contain five elements. Exact finite computation suffices because the domain is finite and all classes were exhaustively enumerated.
residual_risks: The complete distribution relies on exhaustive integer cyclotomic enumeration rather than a short symbolic closed form; the Python script itself was inspected, and a separate implementation was executed.
No statement about arbitrary orders, noise conditioning, or asymptotic families is proved.

value.rationale: The natural fixed-order five-frequency interpolation problem for squarefree Z/15Z has a complete, nontrivial exact rank-incidence invariant. The exact counts distinguish recoverability and losses of one, two or three independent modes; subgroup-defect characterization is a reusable structural boundary. Finite classification is mathematically meaningful even without an all-order theorem.
residual_risks: Only one order and five-frequency sample size are addressed.

limitations: Finite closed census, not an all-order Fourier full-spark criterion.
